architecture: Runtime target: the user runs `pi`, which is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current\pi.cmd` shelling to `node .../pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/cli.js` (single esbuild bundle, version 0.85.1). The bundle also serves the peer packages @earendil-works/pi-tui, /pi-ai, /pi-agent-core, typebox as *virtual modules* (chunk-JVUZSMYM.js:1066) — no such directories exist under node_modules, so runtime imports work but TypeScript types for pi-tui are not on disk. Extensions are jiti-loaded TS modules discovered from ~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts|*/index.ts, .pi/extensions/..., settings `packages` entries, or a package's `pi.extensions` manifest. The extension talks to the host only through ExtensionAPI (events + registrations) and per-call ExtensionContext/ExtensionCommandContext; the host owns the model turn, the TUI and the session file. Consequently the pi-discover rewrite has two viable orchestration strategies inside one extension process: (a) in-process, no-session model calls via ctx.modelRegistry.complete(model, context, options) or ctx.modelRegistry.getProvider(p).streamSimple(...) (scholar's approach: bounded tool loop, own AbortController, Promise.all concurrency), or (b) spawn sibling `pi --mode json -p --no-session --model X --tools ... [--append-system-prompt file] "Task: ..."` child processes and parse JSONL (the bundled subagent example). The user-visible surface is the `/discover` command plus a CustomEditor input lock and footer/widget progress; a final Markdown note is written directly to the vault by the extension, and/or the answer can be injected with pi.sendMessage({triggerTurn:true}) so Pi renders it as an assistant message.

## 2. scholar: exact ExtensionAPI calls at registration

`scholar/index.ts` default factory receives `pi: ExtensionAPI`. It registers **1 command and 2 tools** (not 11):

- Command — `index.ts:490`:
```ts
pi.registerCommand("scholar", {
  description: "Select a PDF book and explicitly start isolated Learn, Exam, or Tutor mode",
  getArgumentCompletions: async (prefix) => ... ,
  handler: (args: string, ctx: ExtensionCommandContext) => { warningContext = ctx; return handleScholarCommand(args, ctx, coordinator); },
});
```
- Tool `scholar` — `tool-controller.ts:830-836`: `pi.registerTool({ name: "scholar", label: "Scholar", description: <long literal>, parameters: ScholarParams, executionMode: "sequential", renderShell: "self", execute(...), renderCall(...) @1241, renderResult(...) @1253 })`.
- Tool `scholar_quiz` — `quiz.ts:509`, name constant `quiz-contract.ts:11` `export const SCHOLAR_QUIZ_TOOL_NAME = "scholar_quiz" as const;`; has `renderCall` @572 and `renderResult` @581.

**Event hooks** (all in `index.ts`): `session_start` :67, `before_agent_start` :86 (returns `{ systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + "\n\n" + instructions }`), `input` :145, `agent_end` :163, `message_update` :171, `tool_execution_start`/`tool_execution_end` :172-173, `agent_settled` :175, `session_shutdown` :256, `message_end` :270, `tool_call` :299 (returns `{ block: true, reason }` to veto), `tool_execution_update` :406, `tool_result` :432 (returns `{ content: [...event.content, {type:"text", text}] }`).

**Never called:** `registerFlag`, `registerShortcut`, `registerProvider`, `registerMessageRenderer`, `registerEntryRenderer`, `registerMarkdownTransformer` (grep for `pi.<that>` across scholar returned nothing).

**Input takeover (`input-lock.ts`, full file read):**
- Mechanism: replace the editor factory with a subclass of Pi's `CustomEditor`, imported from the SDK:
```ts
import { CustomEditor, type ExtensionContext, type ExtensionUIContext } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import { matchesKey, truncateToWidth, type EditorTheme, type KeybindingsManager, type TUI } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";

class ScholarLockedEditor extends CustomEditor {
  handleInput(data: string): void {
    if (this.appKeys.matches(data, "app.interrupt") || matchesKey(data, "escape")) this.interrupt();
  }
  render(width: number): string[] {
    return [this.borderColor(truncateToWidth(` Scholar · ${this.label()} · input paused · Esc interrupts `, Math.max(1, width), ""))];
  }
}
```
- Guard (throws if unavailable):
```ts
if (typeof ui?.setEditorComponent !== "function" || typeof ui?.getEditorComponent !== "function")
  throw new Error("Scholar requires Pi's getEditorComponent/setEditorComponent APIs to pause interactive chat input. Update to a compatible Pi host and restart, then retry.");
```
- Acquire: `currentFactory = ui.getEditorComponent()`; push a `Symbol("scholar-input-lock")` token; on first token set `lockUi`, `previousEditorFactory`, `installedEditorFactory = (tui, theme, keybindings) => new ScholarLockedEditor(...)`; then `ui.setEditorComponent(installedEditorFactory)` and verify `ui.getEditorComponent() === installedEditorFactory`.
- Release returns an idempotent closure; the prior factory is restored only when the last token releases **and** `restoreUi.getEditorComponent() === installedFactory`. `releaseAllInputLocks()` clears the map and restores. Default label literal is `"loading"`.
- The lock additionally swallows non-key input because `render()` shows only the paused line; `interrupt` calls `ctx.abort()`.
- The `input` hook is a second layer: on a busy run it re-inserts the draft with `ctx.ui.setEditorText(event.text)` and returns `{ action: "handled" as const }`.

## 4. scholar: how it runs its own model calls

No SDK session, no child process, no `subagent` API. It calls the **active registry in-process**, which is what preserves Pi's providers, OAuth, headers and credentials (comment at `review-runtime.ts:165-168`).

Signatures (`SDK/dist/core/model-registry.d.ts`):
```ts
complete<TApi extends Api>(model: Model<TApi>, context: Context, options?: ModelsApiStreamOptions<TApi>): Promise<AssistantMessage>;
getProvider(provider: string): Provider | undefined;
getApiKeyAndHeaders(model: Model<Api>): Promise<ResolvedRequestAuth>;   // {ok:true, apiKey?, headers?, baseUrl?, env?} | {ok:false, error}
```
- Non-reasoning path — `review-runtime.ts:298-301`:
```ts
response = await abortable(
  Promise.race([options.modelRegistry.complete(options.model, context, requestOptions), stallPromise]),
  signal,
);
```
with `requestOptions = { signal, maxTokens, timeoutMs, maxRetries: 0, sessionId: requestSessionId, transport: "sse" as const }` (`:296`).
- Reasoning path — `review-runtime.ts:318-321` + stream consumption at `:355-359`:
```ts
const provider = options.modelRegistry.getProvider!(options.model.provider);
const auth = await options.modelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders!(options.model, signal);
const stream = provider.streamSimple(requestModel, context, { ...requestOptions, apiKey, headers, env, reasoning });
[response] = await abortable(Promise.all([Promise.race([stream.result(), stallPromise]), observe()]), signal);
```
- It builds its own `Context` (`{ systemPrompt, messages: [{role:"user", content: prompt, timestamp}], tools: [{name, description, parameters}] }` @:239-243), runs a bounded tool loop (`maxTurns`, `maxToolCalls`, `Value.Check` arg validation, `review-runtime.ts:439-470`), aborts with its own `AbortController`, and finally `cleanupSessionResources(requestSessionId)` (`:3`, `:468`).
- **Parallelism** is plain JS: `review-layer.ts:546`
```ts
await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, packets.length) }, worker));
```
- **Alternative (bundled example, not used by scholar):** `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts` spawns a child `pi` per worker — args built at `:303`: `["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session", ...("--model" ?), ...("--thinking" ?), ...("--tools" ?), "--append-system-prompt", tmpPromptPath, `Task: ${task}`]` — parses JSONL `message_end` events, `MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS = 8`, `MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4`.
- **Third option (SDK docs):** `createAgentSession({ model, tools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), modelRuntime })` → `session.prompt(text, options)`, `session.subscribe(listener)`, `session.steer/followUp`, `session.abort()` — plus `createAgentSessionRuntime()` for new/switch/fork/import. `AgentSession` has no session-replacement methods; those live on `AgentSessionRuntime`.

**No `subagent`/`spawnSubagent` API exists on the host.** Checked: `grep -i 'subagent|Subagent|subAgent|runSubagent'` over the whole `SDK/dist` tree returned **no matches**.

## 5. Session open / resume / switch and extension state lifecycle

**From an extension, session control lives on `ExtensionCommandContext`** (`SDK/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts`, interface declared after `ExtensionContext`):
```ts
newSession(options?: { parentSession?: string; setup?: (sessionManager: SessionManager) => Promise<void>; withSession?: (ctx: ReplacedSessionContext) => Promise<void>; }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
fork(entryId: string, options?: { position?: "before" | "at"; withSession?: ... }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
navigateTree(targetId: string, options?: { summarize?; customInstructions?; replaceInstructions?; label? }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
switchSession(sessionPath: string, options?: { withSession?: ... }): Promise<{ cancelled: boolean }>;
reload(): Promise<void>;
waitForIdle(): Promise<void>;
getSystemPromptOptions(): BuildSystemPromptOptions;
```
`ReplacedSessionContext extends ExtensionCommandContext` and adds `sendMessage(...)` / `sendUserMessage(...)`.

**Events (`ExtensionAPI.on` overloads at `types.d.ts:907-942`; payloads defined above it):**
- `SessionStartEvent` — `reason: "startup" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"`, `previousSessionFile?`.
- `SessionBeforeSwitchEvent` — `reason: "new" | "resume"`, `targetSessionFile?` (cancellable via `SessionBeforeSwitchResult`).
- `SessionShutdownEvent` — `reason: "quit" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"`, `targetSessionFile?`.
- Also `session_before_fork`, `session_before_compact`/`session_compact`/`session_compact_failed`, `session_before_tree`/`session_tree`, `session_info_changed`, `resources_discover` (`reason: "startup" | "reload"`).

**Documented semantics (docs/extensions.md):**
- `:431-433` — "After a successful switch or new-session action, pi emits `session_shutdown` for the old extension instance, reloads and rebinds extensions for the new session, then emits `session_start` with `reason: "new" | "resume"` and `previousSessionFile`."
- `:449-450` — same for fork/clone with `reason: "fork"`.
- `:224` — "Register an idempotent `session_shutdown` handler to close any session-scoped resources you start." Factories may run without a session; do not start background resources from the factory.
- `:1303-1325` — `ctx.reload()` runs the same flow as `/reload`: emits `session_shutdown`, reloads resources, emits `session_start {reason:"reload"}`; the running handler continues in the **old** call frame and must treat reload as terminal (`await ctx.reload(); return;`).
- `:1264-1269` — `withSession` runs only after the old session's `session_shutdown`, runtime teardown, rebind and the new instance's `session_start`; old `pi`/`ctx` are stale; only the passed `ctx` is safe.

**Persistence of extension state:**
- Write: `pi.appendEntry<T>(customType: string, data?: T): void` (`types.d.ts`, ExtensionAPI) — custom entries are NOT in LLM context. scholar uses it at `runtime-coordinator.ts:463` with `SCHOLAR_SESSION_STATE_TYPE = "scholar-active-v3"` (`runtime-session.ts:11`).
- Restore: iterate `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` / `getEntries()` in `session_start`. `ReadonlySessionManager` (`session-manager.d.ts:140`) exposes `getCwd|getSessionDir|getSessionId|getSessionFile (@:209)|getLeafId(@:240)|getLeafEntry|getEntry|getLabel|getBranch(@:262)|buildContextEntries|getHeader|getEntries(@:282)|getTree|getSessionName`.
- scholar's `session_start` handler (`index.ts:67-84`) resets everything: `releaseAllInputLocks()`, `deactivateSession()`, `runtimeSession.reset()`, `toolController.resetTransientState()`; and `session_shutdown` (`:256-268`) releases every run/lock and calls `ctx.ui.setWorkingMessage()`.

## Implications for the pi-discover rewrite (facts only)

1. Runtime target = the bundled CLI (`dist/bundle/cli.js`, v0.85.1) invoked by `pi.cmd`; the extension is a jiti-loaded TS module, so no build step is needed to run it.
2. There is **no host-provided subagent/concurrency API**. Concurrency must be authored in the extension via either `ctx.modelRegistry.complete` / `provider.streamSimple` with `Promise.all` (scholar's pattern, in-process, no session file) or spawned `pi --mode json -p --no-session` workers (subagent example).
3. `ModelRegistry.complete` / `streamSimple` require a `Model` (from `ctx.modelRegistry.find()`/`getAvailable()`, or `ctx.model`) and a hand-built `Context`; `getApiKeyAndHeaders` + `getProvider` are needed to preserve OAuth/custom headers/reasoning mapping.
4. The input box is owned by swapping `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent(factory)` with a `CustomEditor` subclass; `ctx.ui.getEditorComponent()` is required to restore; Esc must be forwarded to `ctx.abort()` (or the extension's own AbortController).
5. Progress uses `ctx.ui.setStatus(key, text)`, `ctx.ui.setWidget(key, factory)`, `ctx.ui.setWorkingMessage(...)`, `ctx.ui.notify(...)`; the working loader row can be customised with `setWorkingIndicator`/`setWorkingVisible`.
6. Final answer: either inject with `pi.sendMessage({ customType, content, display }, { triggerTurn: true })` so Pi renders the assistant turn, or render rich markdown in a tool `renderResult`/`ctx.ui.custom`/`setWidget` using pi-tui `Markdown` + `getMarkdownTheme()`.
7. Sessions: replacement flows (`newSession`/`switchSession`/`fork`) tear down the extension runtime (`session_shutdown`) and reload it (`session_start` with a new reason); any in-memory orchestration state must be re-derived from `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` or `pi.appendEntry`/`getEntries`.
8. Testing/type-checking note: pi-tui / pi-ai have no on-disk `node_modules` here; scholar's own tests work around this by aliasing `@earendil-works/pi-tui` to a resolved path and `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` to `dist/index.js` through jiti (`scholar/tests/verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs:11-18`, `scholar/tests/sdk.mjs:77-82`).
